newsitem.title: DUBAI: 43 FIRMS SHORTLISTED TO TENDER FOR SAUDI PORTS.
newsitem.headline: 43 FIRMS SHORTLISTED TO TENDER FOR SAUDI PORTS.

text.p: Forty three private sector firms have been shortlisted to bid for six projects to operate, manage and maintain docks and equipment used by Saudi Arabia's ports authority, a Saudi newspaper said on Tuesday.

The projects, to be run on a commercial basis for a leasing period of 10 years, will be tendered over the next three months under a gradual plan unveiled late last month, said the business daily al-Eqtisadiah.
The projects are part of efforts to provide more investment opportunities for the private sector in running and operating the kingdom's public establishments, officials have said.
Previous leases of Saudi's dry docks ran up to five years, the newspaper said. "A ten year lease is an adequate incentive for investors to regain their investments," it added.
Saudi ports generated 558 million riyals ($147 million) in profits and handled 80 million tonnes in 1995.
The Saudi Ports Authority would retain its supervisory role over ports on the Red Sea and Gulf coasts and ensure there would be no new price rises in handling fees.
More Saudi nationals would be employed under the plan endorsed by King Fahd.

The six projects include terminals for cargo and bulk wheat imports at the eastern ports of Dammam and Jubail, roll-on roll-off (RORO) goods terminal at Jeddah and the management and operation of the King Fahd ship repair complex.

Jeddah handles mearly one million containers a year, making it the kingdom's busiest port. It is to take delivery of 10 new cranes and two tugs to service large ships lates this year as part of efforts to improve productivity.
Saudi Arabia's 1995-2000 development plan is focusing on operating efficiency of transport service facilities after developing a modern infrastructure.
